title: A crawler pays per page: two separate Cloudflare variants
caption: Two variants that do not share a settlement path. Solid lines, variant (a): the Monetization Gateway closed beta (2026-09-30) uses an x402 V2 402 exchange and settles USDC on Base through Coinbase's x402 facilitator. Dashed lines, variant (b): the credit-backed batch-settlement binding on the cloudflare:402 network, where the crawler signs with RFC 9421 and Cloudflare, as merchant of record, bills and pays out later over off-chain rails.
alt: Flowchart with two variants. In variant (a), drawn with solid lines, the crawler receives a 402 from the Cloudflare edge and retries with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header; the edge calls verify and settle on the Coinbase x402 facilitator, which settles a USDC transfer on Base. In variant (b), drawn with dashed lines, the crawler sends an RFC 9421 signature plus a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE with payTo merchant and asset USD; the edge fetches the key from the crawler's key directory at /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory and records a commitment with Cloudflare billing, with no chain transaction; Cloudflare billing sends a periodic invoice to the crawler and a periodic payout over off-chain rails to the publisher. In both variants the edge serves the page from the publisher origin.

sourceOfTruth.label: x402 batch-settlement on cloudflare:402 (v1.0.0) and Cloudflare's Monetization Gateway beta post (2026-09-30)
